question.text: Deccan Venture Fund is being structured as a new Cat I AIF. The sponsor asks about structural constraints under SEBI (AIF) Regulations. Which of the following is CORRECT?

answer.text: Cat I and Cat II AIFs shall be structured as CLOSED-ENDED funds, and a closed-ended AIF generally has a MINIMUM tenure of 3 years
Cat I and Cat II AIFs must be structured as OPEN-ENDED funds with daily redemption
Cat I AIFs can be open-ended; only Cat II AIFs must be closed-ended
Minimum tenure is 1 year for all categories

explanation.text: The Logic: Per SEBI (AIF) Regulations 2012, Category I and II AIFs SHALL be structured as CLOSED-ENDED funds. A closed-ended AIF generally has a minimum tenure of 3 years. Conditions applicable for redemptions are disclosed in the PPM. This closed-ended structure aligns with the illiquid nature of private-market investments (PE/VC/Infra/Debt) that Cat I/II typically makes. The Trap: The open-ended option inverts the structure (Cat I/II are NEVER open-ended). The Cat I-vs-Cat II distinction option invents a rule. The 1-year option understates the 3-year floor. Note: Cat III AIFs CAN be open-ended — that's the structural contrast. Cross-Exam Context: XIX-C covers structural rules across all categories. XIX-B (Cat III Distributor) tests open-ended Cat III. XXI-B (Portfolio Manager) has no closed/open-ended concept — PMS is a managed account, not a fund.
